classification.difficultyReason: Recognise perpendicular diameters as a way to locate an inscribed square, then use the prescribed central-angle bisections and extend them to obtain eight equally spaced points.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a circle with centre $O$. Draw a square $ABCD$ whose vertices lie on the circle.

answer.short: A square inscribed in the circle, with $AC$ and $BD$ perpendicular diameters.
answer.worked: Draw a circle with centre $O$ and a diameter $AC$. Using equal-radius compass arcs centred at $A$ and $C$, construct the perpendicular bisector of $AC$. Label its intersections with the circle $B$ and $D$, in cyclic order $A,B,C,D$. Join $AB$, $BC$, $CD$ and $DA$. The perpendicular diameters divide the circle into four equal sectors, so the four chords are equal. Each interior angle of $ABCD$ is $90^\circ$, giving a square.

spec.description: Authored sample square inscribed in a circle, with perpendicular diameters through its centre.
spec.mathematics: A, B, C and D occur successively around the circle; AC and BD are perpendicular diameters.

answer.short: Each $90^\circ$ angle is divided into two $45^\circ$ angles.
answer.worked: With equal compass radii centred at $A$ and $B$, draw intersecting arcs inside $\angle AOB$. Draw the ray from $O$ through their intersection. Repeat with equal-radius arcs centred at $B$ and $C$ inside $\angle BOC$. Each new ray bisects its $90^\circ$ angle into two $45^\circ$ angles.

spec.description: The same inscribed square, with compass arcs and rays bisecting the two adjacent central right angles.
spec.mathematics: The constructed rays make angles of 45 and 135 degrees with OA. Each pair of dashed arcs has equal radius.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Hence, find eight points equally spaced around the circle.

answer.short: The four square vertices and the four intersections of the extended bisectors with the circle give eight points, separated by central angles of $45^\circ$.
answer.worked: Extend both bisectors from part b through $O$ to meet the opposite side of the circle. Together with $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$, their four circle intersections give eight points. Successive central angles are all $45^\circ$, so the points are equally spaced around the circle.

spec.description: Completed shared construction showing eight marked circle points and both bisectors extended through the centre.
spec.mathematics: Eight points lie at successive central angular intervals of 45 degrees.
